name: Beef Rissoles with Gravy
steps: Grate one brown onion into a large bowl. Add the beef mince, crushed garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, tomato sauce and 1 tablespoon of the worcestershire sauce. Season with salt and pepper and mix by hand until just combined - don't overwork it or the rissoles turn firm.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into 8 thick rissoles. Keep them chunky rather than flattening them like burgers so they hold their juices.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Brown the rissoles in two batches so they don't crowd the pan, about 3 minutes each side, then transfer to a plate. They don't need to be cooked through yet.
Thinly slice the remaining onion. Melt the butter in the same pan and cook the onion for about 5 minutes until soft and golden, scraping up any browned bits.
Stir the plain flour into the onions and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock and the remaining tablespoon of worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the gravy starts to thicken.
Return the rissoles and any resting juices to the pan. Simmer gently over low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the rissoles are cooked through and the gravy is thick and glossy.
Spoon the onion gravy generously over the rissoles and serve hot, straight from the pan.
